title: Balanced Tofu Rainbow Bowl
subtitle: with Brown Rice, Gochujang and Sesame
description: Our 'balanced' recipes are just that – high in nutritive value (that's fibre-rich veggies, lean proteins and wholegrains, just between us), so these dishes are good for you in every which way! They're perfect for anyone looking to minimise their intake of refined foods without sacrificing on taste.

steps.text: Cook rice: Fill a medium saucepan three-quarters full with water and bring to the boil. Add the rice and cook for 25-27 mins until tender. Drain.
Prep ingredients: Meanwhile, thinly slice the cucumber. Coarsely chop the Chinese broccoli. Shred the carrot using a julienne peeler or coarsely grate with a box grater. Quarter the tofu pieces.

Warm tofu: Heat 2 tsp vegetable oil in a medium deep frypan over medium-high heat. Stir-fry the Chinese broccoli for 2-3 mins until the stems are almost tender. Add the tofu and stir-fry for 1-2 mins until warmed through. Remove from the pan.

Fry eggs: Heat 2 tsp vegetable oil in the same pan over medium-high heat. Crack 2 eggs into the pan and cook for 2-3 mins until the eggs are crisp underneath and the yolks are just set. Remove the pan from the heat.

Serve up: Divide the rice among bowls and top with the cucumber, carrot and Chinese broccoli and tofu. Drizzle with 2 tbs soy sauce and top with the chilli paste (see Kitchen notes) and fried eggs. Scatter over the sesame seeds and enjoy!

Kitchen notes: Korean chilli paste (known as gochujang) is slightly sweet, earthy and has a chilli kick. If you aren't keen on too much heat, serve it at the table for those who like it. ~ This is our take on the Korean dish bibimbap. The word 'bibimbap' translates to 'mixed rice' so make sure you mix everything together before enjoying!
